title: Paranormal Investigator Shares Signs Something Is Haunted, Believes Spirits 'Still Contain Normal Human Emotions' (Exclusive)
excerpt: Beckie-Ann Galentine has had a fascination with paranormal activity since she was a teenager
content:
NEED TO KNOW

  • Mortician and paranormal investigator Beckie-Ann Galentine says unexplained noises, missing objects and opening doors can signal unusual activity

  • Galentine says investigators often find ordinary explanations after speaking with property owners about their experiences

  • She encourages patience over fear, saying perceived spirit anger may be confusion or a different form of communication

Ghostbusters asks, “Who you gonna call?” Well, if you have consistent, unexplained, possibly paranormal activity, you might want to call Beckie-Ann Galentine. 

Galentine — a trained mortician and embalmer — has worked as a paranormal investigator since 2020. The 36-year-old, who takes a “grounded, grief-centered approach to the paranormal,” tells PEOPLE that “if you feel like something is haunted,” that’s usually a good place to start.

“Unexplained noises, disembodied voices, doors opening without being explained, objects going missing over and over again,” she says of warning signs. “You’ll see in a lot of these, especially the hotels that I focus on, where an object was placed out and then it goes missing.”

Also, she jokes that “seeing a ghost is a good sign that a place might be haunted.”

“There are also some really interesting experiences that people have, I guess, in some ways, like, adopted a memory from something in the past,” she continues. “I always think that’s really cool, where people describe experiences where they enter a location, and they absorb some memory from a different life or they get information; they have this knowledge of things.”

She shares that “it’s just boiled down to experiences that you can explain that should not be happening.”

“The door, you lock it and it somehow unlocks and opens again,” she offers. “You put in these preventative measures and you try to reduce it to something, but eventually, people reach a point where they say, ‘I can’t explain this away anymore, and I am here where I’m at in this situation, and it’s haunted, I can’t get past this.’ ” 

She says that when she gets called to investigate, “it’s really about connecting with the living way more than the dead.”

“You work with the people who live or own the property, and they’ll explain to you what their phenomena is that leads them to believe it to be haunted. And hopefully, most of the time, you find very, very normal explanations for those reasons,” Galentine shares. 

She notes that before someone calls about a potentially haunted dwelling, they should look into electricity, wiring or plumbing first, given one of those issues is often the answer.

However, in the case that something cannot be explained away, that’s when she steps in. Galentine says people often think spirits are inevitably “angry” — but she believes that isn’t necessarily the case.

Despite her profession, Galentine notes that she is “a paranormal investigator that will never definitively say that we have absolute evidence of the paranormal, so speaking in absolutes is something I stray from.”

“However, if we are, in theory, imagining dead human spirits as what we’re communicating with people who passed away, I think they could still contain normal human emotions,” she says.

Yet since they aren’t “flesh and bone,” she suggests that their emotions “may not translate the same way either.”

“We’re seeing spirits, and they might just be saying hello, but their way of saying hello was knocking down a glass and it smashed everywhere. Then you’re like, ‘Oh, it’s so angry,’” she says.

With this in mind, she always tries to lead and investigate with “patience and understanding.” 

“A lot of times when you’re called to investigate, people come with this preconceived notion that, ‘There’s something angry in my house. It’s attacking me.’ You have to take what they’re saying and understand the actions, the tangible facts, and remove the bias of their perception or any emotion they’ve applied, because they might say there’s a sad spirit, an angry spirit, but that information is gonna affect the way that you investigate,” Galentine shares. “If you’re told it’s angry, you’re gonna go in fighting fire with fire and attempting to confront the anger.”

Sometimes, she has to investigate further to better understand what the spirit might be reacting to.

“You have to say, ‘Maybe this anger is something else that’s misplaced. Maybe this anger is confusion. They don’t know they’re dead or there’s something missing or something’s being done they don’t like. Or maybe it is like a glass breaks, a door slams, and you’re projecting your living emotions and applying that,’” she explains. “If I break a glass and I slam a door, you’re going to assume I’m angry, but you have to take that bias away and say that might be the only way they know how to communicate.”

Galentine notes that “there are places that are dormant for five years or 10 years without any reports of activity, and then all of a sudden, some change reignites it,” indicating that the spirit wants attention for an unknown reason.
